newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin welcomes CFTC move on cheese mart, milk.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin welcomes CFTC move on cheese mart, milk.

text.p: Wisconsin Governor Tommy Thompson on Thursday welcomed a decision by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to approve milk futures trading and provide federal oversight of the National Cheese Exchange.

The CFTC earlier approved a request by the New York Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange to trade milk futures and options, a move backed by Wisconsin dairy producers in part to draw the Green Bay-based cheese exchange under regulation.
"The CFTC actions will help restore public confidence in the National Cheese Exchange and provide federal oversight over the trading of dairy products," Thompson said.
Dairy farmers have long alleged that the tiny cheese exchange is dominated by a few huge processing companies in a tightly knit club setting cheese prices.

But on Thursday the CFTC said that participation in the National Cheese Exchange was accessible and unimpeded, trading activity was transparent, and record-keeping sufficient for the commission to oversee trading.
Thompson said the U.S. Department of Agriculture should follow the CFTC's regulatory lead "by disconnecting the National Cheese Exchange from the price of milk."
The CSCE contract on Basic Formula Price Milk will be the first cash-settled futures contract in the dairy industry.
